Nano-bananavsCode-rendered

Same Grade 1 English lesson — “Pinky day out” — made two ways. One is painted pixel-by-pixel by an image AI. The other is written as HTML/CSS and rendered by headless Chrome. Here's exactly how they differ.

ایک ہی سبق، دو طریقے — ایک AI امیج، دوسرا کوڈ سے بنی تصویر۔ نیچے مکمل موازنہ دیکھیں۔

🎨 nano-banana ≈ $0.039 / image ⚙️ code-render ≈ $0.00–0.015 / image 🔤 Urdu/Sindhi text: painted vs real fonts

HTML/CSS/SVG (plus the reference art) rendered to PNG by headless Chrome. No image AI.

≈Art is reused/SVG — clean and professional, but less freehand variety than the AI.
The deciding factor

For Urdu & Sindhi, text quality settles it

Our lessons are text-heavy and multilingual. An image AI paints the letters, so non-Latin scripts come out misspelled or with broken joins. Code renders the exact same text with real font glyphs — every time.

اردو اور سندھی متن میں یہی سب سے بڑا فرق ہے — کوڈ ہر بار درست حروف دکھاتا ہے۔

🍌 nano-banana · painted text
پنکی کا دِن
Letters can drift, break, or misspell — risk grows with amount of text.
⚙️ code-rendered · real glyphs
پنکی کا دن
Actual font — correct spelling, joins and RTL, guaranteed.

The verdict

Code-rendered wins for our lesson plans

For multilingual, text-heavy lesson plans, code-rendered images win on text correctness, consistency, editability and — in the cheapest modes — cost. nano-banana's real strength is richer freehand artwork, but it mis-renders Urdu/Sindhi and bills per image. Pick the tool by what a given job needs most:

اردو/سندھی سبقوں کے لیے کوڈ سے بنی تصویر بہتر ہے — درست متن، کم لاگت، اور قابلِ ترمیم۔

✓ Recommended

Methodology & honesty. Measured on this repo: template render latency (~1.6 s), few-shot size (~7.9k tokens), rich-lesson HTML (~10k tokens). Estimated: per-lesson Claude cost (token estimates × published Anthropic pricing) and nano-banana cost/latency (external figures — not benchmarked here). nano-banana reference price ≈ $0.039/image (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image). Run npm run benchmark with an API key to replace estimates with live figures. The reference lesson shown here was itself generated by nano-banana; the code-rendered page reuses the exact reference art so the comparison isolates text & layout rendering.
